trials.notes: Used WP_HTML_Processor::create_fragment(), walked tokens with documented depth boundaries, accepted only string href values, and concatenated get_modifiable_text() only for #text tokens. All called HTML API methods are documented and execution reported no _doing_it_wrong records.

Correct processor and fully documented API surface. The nested subtree walk follows the depth >= recipe and is correct here, though the docs generally prefer a single stateful token loop for repeated regions. Edge semantics for valueless href and decoded text were handled well.

Correct processor and no undocumented API usage. The single-pass closer-driven state machine matches the documented guarantee that HTML Processor visits closers, including end-of-input virtual closers. It does not use depth or breadcrumbs, but that is acceptable for this element-specific capture.

failure_analysis: No trial failed any frozen hidden case: all three passed 8/8, and none produced _doing_it_wrong records. The docs did well in three places: the processor-choice guidance in WP_HTML_Processor Overview / Supported elements steered all subjects to create_fragment() instead of the Tag Processor; the Recipe: collect DOM-style text from a subtree plus get_current_depth() docs taught the #text + get_modifiable_text() pattern; and get_attribute() documented the string|true|null contract clearly enough that all candidates used is_string() and excluded valueless href. The next_token() docs also helped with malformed input by explaining that the HTML Processor visits closing tokens for unclosed elements at end of input. Near-misses: trial-2 used a nested walk despite the repeated-region warning, but its boundary token was only the anchor closer, so it did not skip a needed region. Trial-3 relied on closer-driven flushing rather than depth; this worked because next_token() documents virtual closers, but that pattern is less directly tied to the subtree text recipe.

doc_gaps.problem: The return type is documented, but the HTML Processor method example does not explicitly contrast missing, valueless, and empty-string attributes in markup syntax.
doc_gaps.suggestion: Add a short example such as href missing => null, href with no value => true, href="" => "", and recommend is_string() when callers require an authored string value.

doc_gaps.location: WP_HTML_Processor::next_token() / Recipe: collect DOM-style text from a subtree
doc_gaps.problem: The docs include both nested subtree walks and a warning against nested loops for repeated regions, which can leave readers unsure when each shape is safe.
doc_gaps.suggestion: Clarify that a bounded inner subtree scan is safe when the caller does not need to process the boundary token, while a single stateful loop is preferred when collecting many sibling regions or when boundary tokens carry work.

doc_gaps.problem: The closer-driven state-machine pattern is shown for DT terms, but not framed as a general read-only extraction alternative to depth-bounded subtree scans.
doc_gaps.suggestion: Add a general note that opener/closer state machines are valid for repeated element extraction because virtual closers are emitted, while depth or breadcrumbs are better when matching arbitrary containment.

doc_gaps.problem: The docs explain #text-only extraction and special elements, but do not explicitly state how replaced or void elements inside text-bearing containers contribute to text.
doc_gaps.suggestion: Add a general text-content example showing inline markup contributing its descendant #text, comments and special-element opener text being excluded by default, and void/replaced elements such as IMG contributing no text unless the caller separately opts into attributes like alt.
